snippet.title: Bank Of America Owed A Retired Cop $2,534. His Lawyer Brought A Moving TRUCK.

snippet.title: Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo customers report outages
snippet.description:
Customers at Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo reported trouble accessing their accounts online Monday.

Thousands of reports appeared on Downdetector, with customers describing problems logging into banking apps, conducting transfers and viewing balances. Chase acknowledged an online banking issue and said it was working to restore service.

Note: Mo News observed no problems with in-person withdrawals or deposits at an NYC Chase branch.

The disruptions follow outages affecting Microsoft and payroll platform Workday, along with Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration outage that temporarily halted departures nationwide. No connection between the incidents has been established. The cause of the banking problems was not immediately clear Monday.

snippet.title: Your Bank App Said “No” — What We Know About the Big Bank Outage
snippet.description:
Monday morning, thousands of people opened their bank app… and couldn’t get in. 📱❌

Users reported problems with Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank on Nov 16, with Zelle and Truist also showing up on Downdetector. Chase alone got nearly 10,000 reports, and most were about logging in.

What caused it? As of the reports, none of the banks had given a reason. And no, there’s no sign it’s connected to last week’s Microsoft 365 outage or the FAA ground stop.

💡 If your app goes down: don’t panic. An app being down doesn’t mean your money is gone. And never share your login with anyone who DMs you offering “help”. Scammers love an outage.

Was YOUR bank down? Tell us in the comments 👇

Story developing. Based on user reports (Downdetector) and news coverage as of Nov 16–17, 2026.
